newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Illinois offers down on supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Illinois offers down on supply.

text.p: Heavy supplies of unsold soymeal in railcars pressured soymeal basis offers in Illinois rail markets on Tuesday, dealers said.
"I hear that there's a lot of meal sitting around in Illinois," said a dealer in the southeast.
Those markets were quoted $2.00 per ton lower, but some dealers said they were trading as much as $5.00 per ton lower.
Soymeal values in export markets also fell off sharply as unsold domestic soymeal is offered in export markets.
"There's so much domestic meal around that it's made more available to the export market," said one river dealer.
Demand from end-users is light and many are still buying on an as-needed basis because of the premium that July CBOT soymeal holds to August.
"People are trying to see what happens with the July/August spread," said an Indiana dealer. "Buyers are going to hand-to-mouth and buying as little as they possibly can."
